thread:
anya: quick heads-up — ran the Mistral-3 quant bakeoff this morning across AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 on CUDA14 + Triton. some weird fallbacks on vLLM and a larger-than-expected accuracy delta for one config.
samir: ok can you paste the short summary numbers?
anya: short summary: base fp16 perf baseline. AWQ(4-bit) perplexity +2.3% vs fp16 on eval set, GPTQ(4-bit) +1.1%, FP8 mixed +0.9% but FP8 latency much better on h100.
li: those deltas sound within usual jitter for some prompts but 2.3% for AWQ is higher than last week's runs. same eval set?
anya: yes same eval set & seed. interestingly AWQ on trt-llm container crashes on long context (8k) with this driver stack, but works under vLLM with kernel fallthrough to CPU (very slow).
evan: got logs? specifically from trt-llm — there was a recent kernel change that hits if CUDA 14 + cuFFT shim present.
anya: pasted truncated log below:
```
[2026-03-18 09:12:03] trt-llm: launching attention kernel
E tensorflow: cuBLAS kernel not available, falling back to generic attention (col-major)
E trt-llm: driverAssert at kernel.cu:412
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
```
ryan: that cublas/cublasLt handshake is the thing. on CUDA14 we saw a change in symbol versioning that made some older TRT kernels select a non-optimized path. leads to the fallthrough you saw.
li: does this reproduce on a clean cuda14 + latest driver image? or only in our trt-llm build with AWQ weights?
anya: reproduced on clean image too (pulled public trt-llm:stable + our quant weights). FWIW, GPTQ artifacts didn't crash but had a tiny perf regression vs earlier drivers.
samir: actionable items: 1) pin to driver 535.x for a quick mitigation, 2) file a compat bug for TRT kernels on CUDA14, 3) add a vLLM config to force strict-kernel-selection so we don't fallback silently.
evan: +1. also add a quick perf matrix to docs: (model, quant, backend) -> latency/throughput/accuracy. helps product picks. can you dump the perf matrix?
anya: small matrix (median 5 runs):
- Mistral-3 fp16 / trt-llm (A100): 0.95 tok/ms, ppl baseline
- Mistral-3 FP8 / trt-llm (H100): 1.42 tok/ms, +0.9% ppl
- Mistral-3 GPTQ4 / vLLM (A100): 0.88 tok/ms, +1.1% ppl
- Mistral-3 AWQ4 / vLLM (A100, cuda14): 0.78 tok/ms, +2.3% ppl (crash on trt-llm long ctx)
li: thanks. can we get more granular on the AWQ failure — is it the attention kernel or KV cache blowup?
anya: logs point to attention kernel. KV sizes look sane. also saw this warning before crash: "ATTN_KERNEL: requested sm < 800, using generic path"
ryan: sounds like kernel selection incorrectly mis-detects SM/compute capability with newer drivers. we should reproduce with env var to force kernel selection: `TRT_FORCE_KERNEL=fast_attention`
samir: try that and also run with `TF32=0` env to see if TF32 heuristics are involved.
evan: to move forward: I'll open a ticket and tag NVIDIA + trt-llm repo. anya can you attach minimal repro (model cfg + quant weight) and the exact image tag?
anya: attaching minimal repro to the ticket: trt-llm:21.4.1, cuda:14.0.1, driver: 540.2, model: mistral-3-awq4.tar.gz (small test chunk), run command below:
```
./run_benchmark --model mistral-3-awq4 --ctx 8192 --batch 1 --backend trt-llm --quant awq4
```
li: for immediate customer-facing recommendations: tell them to prefer GPTQ4 on CUDA14 for now if they need stability, or use FP8 on H100 if latency is the priority. AWQ on trt-llm should be flagged experimental.
ryan: agree. also update our model catalog page with that compatibility note and include the perf matrix.
anya: one more oddity — AWQ eval outputs had more short-token repetition for some prompts. not sure if quantization or kernel fallback contributed.
evan: can you run AWQ on the same hardware but force single-threaded kernel so we can isolate numerical vs concurrency effects? small check: `NUMA_AFFINITY=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`
anya: will run and post results here later today.
irma-bot: automated note: created ticket #ML-1248 trt-llm kernel fallback on CUDA14 for AWQ; assigned to evan.
samir: perfect. let's reconvene after the repro and single-thread tests. :thumbsup:
anya: thanks all — will update once I have the single-thread numbers and the pinned-driver smoke test results.
